question: Should `claws update` and `openclaw.clawUpdatePlan.v1` become the experimental core consent boundary for grouped Claw updates?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent, but it creates a new core lifecycle and public CLI/JSON surface whose durability, blind spots, and ownership model require explicit RFC-level maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve the planning contract
options.body: Accept this gated read-only planner as the authoritative consent boundary and land the stack in dependency order after final validation.

options.title: Narrow the public surface
options.body: Keep the reconciliation logic but reduce or internalize the CLI and versioned JSON contract until its durable shape is settled.

options.title: Pause the update stack
options.body: Leave this draft and its dependent executor unmerged until the Claws RFC direction is resolved.

recommendation.title: Approve the planning contract
recommendation.body: Accept this gated read-only planner as the authoritative consent boundary and land the stack in dependency order after final validation.
